caption:
Your text-back looks like spam.

The reason: wrong number.

Many follow-up tools fire that first text from a toll-free or short-code number. It reads like spam because the number doesn't match the business the customer just called, so carriers filter it or customers ignore it.

A local, 10-digit number matching the customer's area code gets opened and answered.

This week: open your text-back tool, check the sending number, and switch it if it isn't local.
